title: Millions of Americans Are Getting Their Extended Warranty Claims DENIED
summary: A warranty-industry exposé walks through real claim denials over maintenance records and part details, a CarShield deceptive-advertising settlement, and a former finance-office seller explaining markups, financing costs, and cancellation rights.

assertions.quote: a claim declined because a customer could produce one maintenance record instead of three
A water pump denied over which hole the coolant came from

verdicts.note: Disputing the precise failure point to argue it falls under an excluded cause is a commonly reported denial tactic in warranty claim disputes

assertions.quote: every product in the finance office has a negative EV

verdicts.note: F&I products are priced to be profitable for the seller, meaning average payout to buyers is necessarily less than premiums collected, consistent with how such products are underwritten

NCLC's loss-ratio analysis finds an implied upper-bound loss ratio below 25% for Etch products and about 10.7% for one major provider's own marketing claim -- most of what's paid for these dealer add-ons isn't returned as claims -- though the finding covers service contracts, GAP, and etch specifically, not every financial product sold in a finance office.

assertions.quote: the company paying claims isn't the one that sold it to you

verdicts.note: Dealer-sold service contracts are typically underwritten and administered by a separate third-party company that pays claims, while the dealer earns a sales commission, a standard industry structure

verdicts.note: Some contracts restrict covered repairs to certain shops, but outright denial for using an independent shop is contract-specific, not universal across providers

CarShield (NRRM, LLC) and its administrator agreed to pay $10 million to settle FTC charges of deceptive advertising about what its vehicle service contracts actually cover.
